name: Ruine Lavant
kurzbeschreibung: The Kirchbichl hill in Lavant is one of the Eastern Alps' most important archaeological sites, featuring late-antique episcopal basilicas and sweeping views.
beschreibung:
Overview

The historic Kirchbichl in Lavant near Lienz is among the most fascinating archaeological sanctuaries in the Eastern Alps. Perched atop a distinctive rocky knoll rising above the sunny Lienz basin, this natural stronghold was continuously inhabited since the Bronze and Iron Ages. During late antiquity, following the decline and destruction of the nearby Roman city of Aguntum in the 5th century AD, the regional Christian population sought refuge upon the fortified Kirchbichl summit, which subsequently flourished as the primary episcopal seat of the region. Extensive archaeological excavations have revealed monumental stone foundations of early Christian basilicas, defensive ramparts, baptisteries, and dwellings, now preserved as an evocative open-air park crowned by the historic pilgrimage church of Saints Peter and Paul.

Route & Requirements

The walking circuit across the Lavanter Kirchbichl is an easy and enriching cultural stroll suited for visitors of all generations. From the village square in Lavant, a well-signposted, gently climbing pathway leads to the hilltop plateau in approximately fifteen to twenty minutes. Comfortable walking shoes are recommended for exploring the gravel trails and grassy grounds surrounding the ancient excavation walls. The trail demands no athletic fitness, making it ideal for families with children and cultural heritage enthusiasts. Bilingual explanatory display boards along the archaeological educational trail vividly recount the construction phases and daily life in antiquity.

Visiting & Getting There

Lavant is located just a few kilometres southeast of Lienz at the foot of the dramatic Lienz Dolomites. It is readily accessible by regional buses from Lienz railway station or via the nearby Dölsach train stop along the Drau Valley line. Motorists will find complimentary parking facilities in Lavant village near the municipal office and sports ground. The archaeological open-air grounds on Kirchbichl are freely accessible throughout the year during daylight hours with no admission fee. Specialised guided walking tours are organised regularly during the summer months in cooperation with the Aguntum Museum.

Tips

The viewpoint by the pilgrimage church affords panoramic vistas across the entire Lienz valley basin and the rugged spires of the Lienz Dolomites. Be sure to pair your excursion with a visit to the nearby Roman City of Aguntum in Dölsach to complete your understanding of Roman life in Tyrol. At the foot of the hill, visitors will also find the scenic Dolomitengolf course, offering lovely walking trails and inviting restaurants.
